parts.problem_md:
Giant African land snails are an invasive species in Florida.

Suggest two other reasons why scientists are concerned about the populations of giant African land snails in Florida.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Any **two** from:
> 
> - They destroy crops
> - They eat native plants and change habitats
> - They out-compete other snails
> - They may have no natural predators
> - They may reproduce rapidly
> - They may spread across Florida or the USA
> - They may spread disease
> 
> **[2 marks]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> - The question says 'other reasons', so 'they are invasive' does not score.

parts.problem_md:
The snails contain 100 units of energy.

![Food-chain diagram showing water hyacinth plant → snail → egret → eagle. The snail box states “100 units”; dotted lines beneath the plant, egret and eagle labels are for entering energy values.](assets/001-food-chain-diagram-showing-water-hyacinth-plant-.png)

*Figure 6.3*

Complete Figure 6.3 to show the units of energy in the food chain.
parts.solution_md:
About 10% of the energy passes from one trophic level to the next.

Water hyacinth plant: 100 × 10 = **1000 units**  **[1 mark]**

Egret: 100 ÷ 10 = **10 units** and eagle: 10 ÷ 10 = **1 unit**  **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> - Work backwards to the producer by multiplying by 10, and forwards to the consumers by dividing by 10.

parts.problem_md:
Figure 6.2 shows a food web containing water hyacinth plants.

![Food web diagram; arrows point from food to feeder. Water hyacinth plant is eaten by weevil, raccoon and snail; weevil by raccoon; snail by egret; and raccoon and egret by eagle.](assets/002-food-web-diagram-arrows-point-from-food-to-feede.png)

*Figure 6.2*

Use Figure 6.2 to identify:

all the primary consumers

the organism that only feeds as a secondary consumer

the organism that feeds at trophic levels two and three
parts.solution_md:
All the primary consumers: **weevil, raccoon and snail**  **[1 mark]**

Only feeds as a secondary consumer: **egret**  **[1 mark]**

Feeds at trophic levels two and three: **raccoon**  **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> - For 'all the primary consumers', you need every one of them for the mark. Check each arrow that leaves the water hyacinth plant.

parts.problem_md:
Complete the sentences about the events that occur in a flower after pollination.

After pollination, the flower is ..........

This allows the formation of fruits and ..........
parts.solution_md:
After pollination, the flower is **fertilised**  **[1 mark]**

This allows the formation of fruits and **seeds**  **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
Water hyacinth plants produce flowers above the surface of the water. These flowers are pollinated by two different methods.

Suggest two ways that water hyacinth flowers are pollinated.
parts.solution_md:
**By insects**  **[1 mark]**

**By wind**  **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> - The flowers are above the water, so water does not carry the pollen. Think about what moves pollen through the air.

Water hyacinth plants reduce the growth of other aquatic plants by competition.

Suggest two ways water hyacinth plants compete with other aquatic plants.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Any **two** from:
> 
> - They compete for light
> - They compete for mineral ions (nutrients)
> - They compete for space
> - They compete for carbon dioxide
> - They compete for oxygen
> 
> **[2 marks]**
